chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abu 'Aqil 'Isa ibn Nasr, said:

Ali ibn Ziyad al-Saymari wrote asking for a shroud, so he wrote back to him: “Indeed, you will need it in the year eighty.” Then he died in the year eighty, and he sent the shroud to him a few days before his death.

key_terms.تَحْتَاجُ: you will need; indicating future necessity
key_terms.سَنَةِ ثَمَانِينَ: the year eighty; the specified year of death
key_terms.فَمَاتَ: then he died; confirming the foretold event
key_terms.كَفَنًا: a burial shroud requested for use after death
key_terms.مَوْتِهِ: his death; the occasion for which the shroud was needed

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the Imam’s knowledge of a companion’s impending death?
ai.summary: This report narrates that 'Ali ibn Ziyad al-Saymari requested a shroud and received a written reply indicating that he would need it in the year eighty. The event occurred exactly as stated, and the shroud was sent shortly before his death, reflecting foreknowledge associated with the Imam عليه السلام.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Abu Aqeel Isa Bin Nasr who said,

‘Ali Bin Ziyad Al-Saymari wrote asking for a shroud. So he wrote to him<sup>asws</sup> (the 12<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) in the year (two hundred and) eighty, and he did die in the year (two hundred and) eighty, and he<sup>asws</sup> sent the shroud to him before his death by two days’.
en.sarwar: 26. Ali ibn Muhammad has said the following.

“Ibn al-‘Ajami in his will had set aside one third of his properties for the holy location (office of the Imam (a.s.) and had written the deed for it. Before he would take the one third out of his properties he gave a certain amount to his son, abu al-Miqdam, of which no one had any knowledge. He (Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) wrote to him, “Where is the property that you set aside for abu al-Miqdam?”
